A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GABP study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The proofs and experimental details can be matched despite appendix renumbering and the added notation appendix.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 1–2 report original simulations comparing convergence and dynamic regret in random-payoff and hard concave-convex games under full and noisy feedback.

after.justification: Section 6 and Figures 1–2 retain original simulation results for both game classes and feedback settings, including revised gap-function results for the hard game.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation (3) retain the same gradient update, boosting perturbation and periodic anchor updates. Changes to stationary-point notation and explanatory prose do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 50-dimensional random-payoff zero-sum games and the 100-dimensional hard concave-convex game, each with full and noisy feedback. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons retain exactly OG, AOG and APGA against GABP in both games and feedback settings. The theoretical comparison table also retains its method membership.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 switch the hard game's evaluation metric from tangent residual to GAP under both feedback settings. Initializations, noise distribution, iteration ranges and the hyperparameters in v1 Table 1/v2 Table 2 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The same full/noisy-feedback comparisons and dynamic-regret analysis are retained. No additional ablation, sensitivity study, robustness scenario, error analysis or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 random-payoff matrices generated with different seeds, 10 seeds for the hard game, and standard-error shading in Figure 1. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Figure 1 replaces the two hard-game tangent-residual trajectories with newly reported GAP trajectories. The random-payoff curves and Figure 2 regret curves remain unchanged. The replacement uses a different metric and does not establish a performance gain over v1.

T1.justification: The full-feedback proof in v2 Appendix B.1 explicitly restricts intermediate residual inequalities to t >= 2. The regret proof changes an intermediate summation's starting index from 3 to 2. These are limited proof-domain and indexing corrections; the main assumptions, theorems and convergence rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same GABP contribution, convergence rates of tilde-O(1/T) and tilde-O(T^(-1/7)), O((ln T)^2) regret bound, and competitive-or-superior empirical performance claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds an explanation connecting GABP's existing advantage over Abe et al. (2024) to anchor-to-stationary-point distance decreasing as O(1/k), versus O(1/sqrt(k)) in that prior analysis. Existing interpretations of noise handling and the bandit-feedback extension remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Introduction footnote 2 adds an implementation-repository link absent from v1. Hardware, game construction and hyperparameter disclosures are otherwise retained in v1 Appendix D/v2 Appendix E.

R1.justification: The added paragraph in Section 4.3 makes the technical distinction from Abe et al. (2024) more explicit through the intermediate convergence-rate comparison. The cited-work set, related-literature section and broader research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a notation appendix, a short comparative explanation and acknowledgments, simplifies stationary-point notation throughout, and makes local wording edits. The main section sequence and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the notation table, redraws Figure 1's hard-game panels with GAP axes and revises its caption. The conference template changes typography and page layout, with existing tables and proofs reflowed; Figure 2 and the existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The main gains are clearer exposition and better reproducibility guidance through the notation table, added convergence explanation and code-access link. Small proof corrections improve precision. Reporting GAP consistently improves Figure 1's coherence but replaces the hard-game residual evidence rather than expanding it. The method, central guarantees and experimental scope remain essentially unchanged.
